# PlantCare101

> Houseplant care guides for 80 indoor plants, each with a watering calculator set to the plant, and six tools: watering calculator, pet-safe plant checker (ASPCA cat and dog lists), plant problem diagnosis, window light finder, fertilizer dilution and pot size. Care figures come from university extension services (NC State, Clemson HGIC, University of Illinois, UF/IFAS), the Missouri Botanical Garden, the RHS and the ASPCA, each cited with the date it was read. Published by Radif Partners. US English.

## Plant guides
- [African violet care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/african-violet/): African violets want bright light without hot afternoon sun, such as a spot within 3 feet of a large window, and a light mix kept barely moist with room-temperature water that never splashes the leaves. Keep nights at 60°F or warmer.
- [Air plant care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/air-plant/): Air plants grow without soil. Soak or drench the whole plant, shake it, let it dry upside down within a few hours, and give bright, filtered light. Clemson suggests a 20 to 30 minute soak weekly; the RHS keeps them above 54°F.
- [Alocasia care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/alocasia/): Give an alocasia bright, indirect light, warmth above 60°F (16°C) and humid air, and water from spring to fall whenever the top 2 inches of compost are dry. In winter, the RHS says to keep it cooler and drier so it can go dormant.
- [Aloe vera care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/aloe-vera/): Grow aloe vera in the sunniest window you have, in gritty cactus mix in a pot with drainage holes. Let the mix dry completely before each watering, water very sparingly in winter, and keep it frost-free, with cool winter nights around 46 to 50°F.
- [Amaryllis care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/amaryllis/): Pot an amaryllis bulb in a pot barely wider than the bulb, with a third to half of it above the mix, give at least four hours of direct sun, and water lightly until growth starts. After flowering, keep the leaves growing, then rest the bulb.
- [Anthurium care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/anthurium/): Anthurium flowers best in bright, indirect light at 65 to 80°F (18 to 27°C) with 60 to 80 percent humidity. Water when the top inch of its airy, bark-rich mix is dry, and keep it away from cold drafts and direct sun.
- [Areca palm care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/areca-palm/): Areca palms need bright, indirect light from an east, west or south window, mix that stays moist but never soggy, and high humidity. Clemson Extension gives ideal temperatures of 65 to 70°F at night and 75 to 85°F by day.
- [Arrowhead plant care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/arrowhead-plant/): Arrowhead plant (Syngonium) grows best in medium to bright indirect light at 65 to 75°F (18 to 24°C). Let the surface of the mix dry slightly between waterings, never completely, and cut back climbing stems if you want to keep the arrow-shaped juvenile leaves.
- [Basil care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/basil/): Basil wants six or more hours of direct sun, warmth above 50°F and a rich mix kept evenly moist, never soggy. Pinch the tips and remove flower buds to keep leaves coming, and treat the plant as an annual you replace each year.
- [Begonia care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/begonia/): Grow begonias in bright light without hot sun, keep the mix evenly moist but never soggy, and hold rooms at 66 to 73°F. Rex begonias also need humid air and careful watering; cane and angel wing begonias forgive far more.
- [Bird of paradise care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/bird-of-paradise/): Give a bird of paradise the brightest spot you have, ideally full sun at a south window. Soak the pot, let the mix dry slightly, feed every two weeks in spring and weekly in summer, and keep nights above 50°F.
- [Bird's nest fern care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/birds-nest-fern/): Keep a bird's nest fern's mix continually moist, pouring water onto the soil around the rosette rather than into the central cup. Give it bright, indirect light such as a north window, temperatures of 60 to 70°F, and extra humidity in winter.
- [Bonsai care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/bonsai/): Indoors, grow a tropical bonsai such as Ficus microcarpa: bright light, compost kept just moist in its shallow pot, warmth of 65°F or more, and a balanced liquid feed in the growing season. Juniper bonsai are outdoor trees that need a winter rest.
- [Boston fern care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/boston-fern/): A Boston fern wants potting mix that stays barely moist and never dries out, bright indirect light with no direct sun, and humid air. Clemson Extension advises half-strength liquid fertilizer once a month from April through September and none in winter.
- [Bromeliads care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/bromeliad/): Bromeliads drink through a cup formed by their leaves: keep a little fresh water in it, flush it often, and water the potting mix only when its top half is dry. Give bright, filtered light and 60°F to 85°F, per Clemson.
- [Burro's tail care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/burros-tail/): Burro's tail needs bright light with some direct sun, gritty mix that dries out between waterings, and a hanging pot where nothing brushes its brittle stems. Water less in winter and feed only once or twice during the growing season.
- [Cactus care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/cactus/): Desert cacti need a south or west window with several hours of direct sun, a free-draining mix, and thorough watering from March to September. In winter, Clemson Extension advises a cool 45 to 55°F (7 to 13°C) rest with just enough water to prevent shriveling.
- [Calathea care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/calathea/): Calatheas want steady conditions: bright but indirect light, a mix kept evenly moist but never soggy, humidity of 60 percent or more, and 65 to 75°F. Water with rainwater or distilled water, since NC State notes that fluoride in tap water browns leaf tips.
- [Cast iron plant care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/cast-iron-plant/): Cast iron plant does best in bright indirect light but tolerates deep shade; direct sun bleaches its leaves. Water regularly from spring to fall, sparingly in winter, and keep it above 50°F, per Missouri Botanical Garden. It needs no extra humidity and little fertilizer.
- [Chinese evergreen care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/chinese-evergreen/): Chinese evergreen thrives in low to medium indirect light between 68 and 77°F (20 and 25°C), watered when the top inch of mix feels dry. Keep it above 55°F (13°C): cold drafts mark the older leaves with dark, greasy patches.
- [Christmas cactus care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/christmas-cactus/): Keep a Christmas cactus in bright, indirect light, water when the top inch of soil feels dry, and feed it monthly at half strength from spring through summer. To bloom, it needs long, dark nights starting in mid-September, as Clemson Extension explains.
- [Coleus care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/coleus/): Grow coleus in bright light, with direct sun only for sun-tolerant cultivars, and water when the top inch of mix is dry without letting the pot dry out. Pinch tips and flower spikes, and bring it indoors before frost.
- [Croton care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/croton/): Give a croton your brightest window, with some direct sun, and water when the top inch of mix is dry. NC State advises generous watering from spring to autumn and sparing watering in winter. Keep it above 50°F and away from drafts.
- [Cyclamen care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/cyclamen/): Keep florist's cyclamen cool, 60 to 65°F by day and around 50°F at night, in bright light without direct sun. Water when the surface is dry, at the pot edge or from below so the tuber stays dry. It goes dormant in summer.
- [Dieffenbachia care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/dieffenbachia/): Dieffenbachia grows best in bright, filtered light at 60 to 75°F (16 to 24°C). Water thoroughly, then wait until the top inch of soil is dry. Every part of the plant is poisonous: the sap can swell the mouth and throat, so keep it away from children and pets.
- [Dracaena care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/dracaena/): Grow corn plant and Madagascar dragon tree in bright, indirect light, water once the surface of the mix feels dry, and keep them between 60 and 75°F. Use fluoride-free water: Clemson Extension calls dracaena very sensitive to fluoride, which burns the leaf tips.
- [Echeveria care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/echeveria/): Echeverias need strong light, a gritty cactus mix and water only once the mix has dried out. The RHS advises keeping them above 50°F (10°C) and resting them in winter with just a light watering every few weeks to stop shriveling.
- [English ivy care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/english-ivy/): Indoors, English ivy wants bright light without direct sun, cool rooms of 50 to 70°F, and water as soon as the top half inch of mix feels dry, per Clemson Extension. Pinch the tips to keep it bushy, watch for spider mites, and keep it away from pets.
- [Ficus Audrey care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/ficus-audrey/): Ficus Audrey wants bright, indirect light and a thorough watering whenever the top 2 to 3 inches of mix feel dry, the rule NC State Extension gives. Keep it between 65 and 80°F (18 and 27°C), at 50 to 80 percent humidity, away from cold drafts.
- [Fiddle-leaf fig care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/fiddle-leaf-fig/): Give a fiddle-leaf fig bright, indirect light with shade from hot afternoon sun, water thoroughly once the top two inches of mix feel dry, and keep it above 55°F, away from drafts and heating vents. Sudden leaf drop usually points to a watering mistake, so check the mix before you pour.
- [Fittonia care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/fittonia/): Keep a fittonia's mix evenly moist, give it bright indirect light from an east or north window, and hold the room above 55°F. It faints flat when dry and revives after watering, but repeated collapses weaken it.
- [Gardenia care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/gardenia/): An indoor gardenia needs bright light without harsh sun, acidic compost kept evenly moist, and high humidity. The RHS gives 70°F to 75°F as the ideal range, never below 60°F. Avoid drafts and sudden temperature changes, which make the buds drop.
- [Haworthia care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/haworthia/): Haworthias want bright light with a few hours of gentle direct sun, though they tolerate dimmer rooms than most succulents. Let the mix dry between waterings, keep them above 50°F (10°C), and give them a cool, drier winter rest.
- [Hibiscus care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/hibiscus/): Tropical hibiscus needs bright light, moist roots while it grows and weekly feeding from spring, per the RHS. Keep winter nights above 45°F (7°C) and expect a semi-dormant rest with some leaf drop. The ASPCA lists hibiscus as non-toxic to cats and dogs.
- [Hoya care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/hoya/): Hoyas want bright light, a chunky mix of potting soil, orchid bark and perlite, and water once the top third to half of the pot has dried. Keep nights above 50°F, never cut off old flower spurs, and the ASPCA lists them as pet safe.
- [Hydrangea care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/hydrangea/): Keep a potted gift hydrangea evenly moist in bright light without hot afternoon sun. When the flowers fade, cut those stems back to a pair of healthy buds, then plant it outdoors in spring or fall in part shade: it is a hardy shrub, not a permanent houseplant.
- [Jade plant care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/jade-plant/): Give a jade plant four or more hours of direct sun a day, water when the mix has nearly dried in spring and summer, and let it dry out between waterings in winter. Use a fast-draining, cactus-type mix and aim for nights around 50 to 55°F.
- [Jasmine care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/jasmine/): Pink jasmine needs at least four hours of direct sun indoors, steady watering while it grows, and cool nights of about 50 to 55°F in winter. Feed with a high-potassium fertilizer in summer and prune right after the late winter flowers fade.
- [Kalanchoe care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/kalanchoe/): Kalanchoe needs bright light, a fast-draining mix and deep watering only after the soil has dried. To bloom again, it needs about six weeks of 14-hour, fully dark nights in fall or winter. The ASPCA lists it as toxic to cats and dogs.
- [Lavender care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/lavender/): Lavender needs at least six hours of direct sun and a gritty, fast-draining mix that dries well between waterings. Indoors only a bright south window or grow lights come close, so most potted lavender does far better outside from spring to fall.
- [Lithops care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/lithops/): Lithops need 4 to 5 hours of morning sun and water only in their growing periods: late spring into early summer, then late summer and fall. Keep them completely dry in winter and early spring while the new leaf pair replaces the old one.
- [Lucky bamboo care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/lucky-bamboo/): Lucky bamboo is a Dracaena, not a bamboo. Grow it in bright, indirect light, either in moist potting mix or in chlorine-free water over pebbles, which NC State Extension says to change weekly. Direct sun scorches the leaves, and chlorinated tap water browns the tips.
- [Maidenhair fern care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/maidenhair-fern/): A maidenhair fern needs mix that stays moist at all times, humidity around 50 percent, and the gentle light of a north window. Keep days at 60 to 70°F with cooler nights. Letting it dry out even once can crisp every frond.
- [Majesty palm care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/majesty-palm/): Majesty palms need bright, indirect light, mix kept consistently moist, high humidity and temperatures between 65 and 85°F, according to NC State Extension. Keep them out of direct sun, which scorches the fronds, and away from cold drafts and heaters.
- [Meyer lemon tree care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/meyer-lemon-tree/): A Meyer lemon tree needs at least 8 hours of sun, a bark-based mix at pH 5.5 to 6.5 and water when the top 2 to 3 inches dry, per Clemson Extension. Winter it in a bright room at 55 to 65°F (13 to 18°C).
- [Mint care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/mint/): Grow mint in its own pot of rich, moist mix, ideally 12 to 16 inches wide, in sun or partial shade. Keep the mix evenly moist, harvest often to keep it bushy, and divide the clump every three to four years.
- [Money tree care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/money-tree/): Give a money tree bright, indirect light, keep its mix moderately and evenly moist without ever letting it stand in water, and hold it between 65 and 75°F. NC State Extension warns that direct sun scorches the leaves and that dry soil makes them drop.
- [Monstera care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/monstera/): Give a monstera bright, indirect light, water thoroughly once the top quarter to third of the mix has dried, and keep it between 65 and 77°F with moderate to high humidity. A moss pole and a heavy pot help it build large, split leaves.
- [Monstera adansonii care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/monstera-adansonii/): Give Monstera adansonii bright, indirect light, water thoroughly once the mix is almost dry, and keep it at 65 to 77°F with high humidity. A moss pole or trellis helps it make bigger, more perforated leaves.
- [Moth orchid care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/orchid/): Grow a moth orchid in bark-based orchid mix, never potting soil, in a bright east window out of direct summer sun. Water about once a week, letting the bark nearly dry, keep it between 61 and 86°F, and cut the spent spike above a node to encourage reblooming.
- [Norfolk Island pine care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/norfolk-island-pine/): Grow a Norfolk Island pine in the brightest window you have, in a cool room around 55 to 65°F, and water it regularly from spring to fall without letting the mix turn soggy. NC State Extension advises watering sparingly in winter and misting in heated rooms.
- [Olive tree care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/olive-tree/): An olive tree needs full sun, 6 or more hours of it according to NC State Extension, gritty free-draining compost and water only when the surface dries. Indoors it rarely flowers unless it spends about 2 months at 40 to 50°F (4 to 10°C) in winter.
- [Oxalis care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/oxalis/): Give oxalis a bright, sunny window, a well-drained mix kept barely moist, and temperatures no higher than about 75°F. When the leaves die back, stop watering and let the bulbs rest in a cool, dark place until new shoots appear.
- [Parlor palm care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/parlor-palm/): Parlor palms grow best in medium, indirect light from a north or east window and tolerate dim rooms. Water thoroughly when the surface of the mix dries, never let the pot dry out completely, and keep the plant above 60°F in winter.
- [Peace lily care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/peace-lily/): Keep a peace lily in bright, indirect light out of direct sun, water when the top of the mix starts to dry so it never wilts hard, and hold it between 68 and 85°F by day. Feed at quarter strength every six to eight weeks in spring and summer.
- [Peperomia care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/peperomia/): Most peperomias want bright, indirect light, a light, well-drained mix and water only once the top of the pot has dried. Keep them above 50°F and out of drafts. Every peperomia the ASPCA lists is non-toxic to cats and dogs.
- [Philodendron care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/philodendron/): Most philodendrons want bright, indirect light, a loose mix watered when the top inch is dry, and warmth: Clemson gives 65 to 70°F at night and 75 to 85°F by day. Heartleaf philodendron tolerates very low light; self-heading types need more light and room.
- [Pilea (Chinese money plant) care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/pilea/): Pilea peperomioides, the Chinese money plant, wants bright indirect light, a moist but well-drained mix that never stays soggy, and a spot away from drafts and heaters. Turn it weekly so it grows straight, and pot up the pups it sends up around the base.
- [Poinsettia care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/poinsettia/): Give a poinsettia bright, indirect light for about six hours a day, keep it between 60 and 70°F away from drafts, and water when the surface feels dry. Reblooming needs about 14 hours of total darkness every night from early fall.
- [Polka dot plant care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/polka-dot-plant/): A polka dot plant needs bright, filtered light to keep its pink or white spots, a mix that stays lightly moist, and regular pinching to stay bushy. Keep it between 65 and 75°F and away from hot afternoon sun.
- [Ponytail palm care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/ponytail-palm/): Ponytail palms want the brightest window you have, a gritty cactus mix, and deep watering only after the mix has dried out completely. Cut watering back sharply in winter. NC State Extension rates the plant hardy to 50°F, so keep it away from cold glass.
- [Pothos care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/pothos/): Pothos grows best in bright, indirect light but tolerates dim rooms. Let the mix dry well between waterings, then soak it so water reaches every root, and keep it between 60 and 85°F. Cut long vines back above a node to keep it full.
- [Prayer plant care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/prayer-plant/): Keep a prayer plant in bright, indirect light, never direct sun, with the mix evenly moist from spring to fall and a little drier in winter. Give it high humidity, monthly feeding in the growing season, and temperatures that stay above 60°F.
- [Rhaphidophora tetrasperma care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/rhaphidophora-tetrasperma/): Rhaphidophora tetrasperma wants bright, indirect light, water once the top inch of mix is dry, temperatures between 65 and 80°F, and humidity around 60%. Give it a moss pole or trellis; it climbs fast and is toxic to pets.
- [Rosemary care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/rosemary/): Grow rosemary in a clay pot of gritty mix, give it at least six hours of sun, and let the top of the mix dry between waterings without ever letting the root ball go bone dry. Indoors in winter, a cool, bright, humid spot works best.
- [Rubber plant care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/rubber-plant/): Grow a rubber plant in bright, indirect light with some morning sun, water when the top of the soil feels slightly dry, and keep it between 60 and 80°F, never below 55°F. Clemson Extension recommends feeding every two weeks in spring and summer.
- [Sago palm care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/sago-palm/): Warning first: every part of a sago palm is poisonous, and the ASPCA says one or two seeds can be fatal to a pet. If no pets or small children can reach it, give it bright filtered light, sandy fast-draining mix and water once the top two inches dry.
- [Schefflera care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/schefflera/): Give a schefflera medium to bright, filtered light, water thoroughly and let the top half inch of soil dry before the next watering, and keep it at 65 to 75°F by day and above 60°F at night, the ranges Clemson Extension recommends.
- [Snake plant care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/snake-plant/): Snake plants want the potting mix to dry out completely before every watering, then a thorough soak until water drains. In winter, NC State Extension advises watering only once every one to two months. Any light works, from a dim hallway to a sunny window.
- [Spider plant care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/spider-plant/): Give a spider plant medium to bright indirect light, let the top inch of soil dry briefly between waterings, and use rainwater or distilled water if your tap water is fluoridated. Clemson Extension puts the ideal daytime range at 65 to 75°F.
- [Staghorn fern care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/staghorn-fern/): Grow a staghorn fern mounted on a board over sphagnum moss in bright, filtered light. Soak the mount when the moss feels nearly dry, never letting it dry out completely, and keep it around 68 to 72°F by day with high humidity.
- [String of bananas care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/string-of-bananas/): String of bananas needs bright, indirect light and a coarse cactus mix. NC State Extension says to water only when the top half of the soil feels dry. It is not full-sun or frost tolerant, and it is toxic to pets if eaten.
- [String of hearts care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/string-of-hearts/): String of hearts wants bright, indirect light and a sandy, fast-draining mix that dries out completely between waterings. NC State notes the plant is dormant in winter, when watering should drop even further. Wide gaps between leaves mean it needs more light.
- [String of pearls care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/string-of-pearls/): Grow string of pearls in a sandy cactus mix in bright light, ideally hanging near an east or west window. Water when the mix has dried well down, but not to dust. NC State advises 70 to 80°F in summer and 50 to 60°F in winter.
- [Succulents care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/succulents/): Succulents need bright light and dry soil: a sunny window, four or more hours of direct sun for jade, and water only after the mix has dried out completely. Plant them in a gritty, fast-draining mix in a pot with drainage holes.
- [Tradescantia care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/tradescantia/): Tradescantia, the inch plant, grows best in bright filtered light with only morning sun, at 65 to 75°F, in a peaty mix watered as the surface dries. Cut it back hard each spring, root the tips, and keep it from pets: the ASPCA lists it as toxic.
- [Venus flytrap care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/venus-flytrap/): Venus flytraps need full sun, a mix that never dries, and only rainwater or distilled water. NC State warns that tap water and fertilizer can kill them. Each winter they need a cool dormancy; Clemson cites at least 45 days below 45°F.
- [Weeping fig care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/weeping-fig/): A weeping fig wants bright light, a mix kept evenly moist in summer and slightly drier in winter, and one spot it never leaves. Clemson Extension puts ideal nights at 65 to 70°F (18 to 21°C). Moving it or chilling it triggers leaf drop.
- [Yucca care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/yucca/): Indoor yucca, here the spineless Yucca gigantea, needs the brightest window you have, a very gritty mix of one part potting soil to three parts perlite or sand, and water only once the pot has dried out. Keep it above 50°F.
- [ZZ plant care](https://plantcare101.com/plants/zz-plant/): Water a ZZ plant only after the potting mix has dried completely, which Clemson Extension says works out to once or twice a month. Give it bright, indirect light if you can and low light if you must, never full sun, and keep it above 60°F.

## Problem guides
- [Brown leaf tips](https://plantcare101.com/guides/brown-leaf-tips/): Brown leaf tips usually mean the leaf edge is the first place salt, fluoride or dry air does damage. Look for a white crust on the soil, think about your water and your heating, then flush the pot with plain water. The brown parts stay brown; new leaves show whether the fix worked.
- [Pests](https://plantcare101.com/guides/houseplant-pests/): Most houseplant pests ride in on a new plant. Spider mites leave pale speckles and fine webbing, fungus gnats are tiny flies breeding in wet mix, and mealybugs look like white cotton in leaf joints. Isolate the plant, treat once a week for several weeks, and let the mix dry out to stop gnats.
- [How often to water](https://plantcare101.com/guides/how-often-to-water-plants/): There is no fixed schedule. Water when the plant's own drying test says so: most houseplants when the top inch or two of mix feels dry, succulents only when the pot is dry throughout. Pot size, clay, light, season and humidity stretch or shorten the interval, which the calculator below estimates.
- [Repotting step by step](https://plantcare101.com/guides/how-to-repot-a-plant/): Repot in spring or early summer, when the plant is growing. Pick a pot 1 or 2 inches wider with a drainage hole, slide the plant out, loosen or cut circling roots, set it at the same depth in fresh potting mix, press gently and water until it drains.
- [Leggy plants](https://plantcare101.com/guides/leggy-plants/): A leggy plant has long, bare stems with small leaves spaced far apart, and the cause is almost always too little light. Move it closer to a window or add a grow light, then cut the stretched stems back above a leaf node. Old stretched growth never tightens up; only new growth does.
- [Overwatering vs underwatering](https://plantcare101.com/guides/overwatering-vs-underwatering/): An overwatered plant droops with soft, limp leaves while its mix is still wet and the pot feels heavy. An underwatered plant droops with dry, crisp leaves in a light pot of dry mix. Feel the mix 2 inches down before adding water: wilting in wet mix means stop watering.
- [Root rot](https://plantcare101.com/guides/root-rot/): Root rot shows as wilting in wet mix, a sour smell, and roots that are brown to black and soft instead of firm. Unpot the plant, rinse the roots, cut every rotten one back to firm tissue and repot in fresh, sterile mix. If most roots are dead, root cuttings instead.
- [Yellow leaves](https://plantcare101.com/guides/yellow-leaves/): Most yellow leaves on a houseplant trace back to too much water: soggy mix starves the roots of oxygen and the plant sheds its oldest leaves first. Push a finger 2 inches into the mix. Wet means stop watering and look at the roots; dry means check light, feeding, pests and age.

## Method
- [How we calculate](https://plantcare101.com/methodology/): watering ranges are estimates built from each plant's drying rule and documented multipliers, never a fixed date.
